title: What is the McKinsey interview process, and how should you prepare?
description: McKinsey's hiring steps explained: application, the Solve assessment, Personal Experience Interviews and interviewer-led cases, with preparation tips.
hook: McKinsey's process has a reputation for being intense, and it is. But it is also well documented and predictable, which means you can prepare for every part of it. Here is what to expect, step by step.
body:
The steps

  1. Online application. CV, and in some offices a cover letter and transcripts.
  2. Solve assessment. For many client-facing roles, McKinsey uses an online, game-based test called Solve. Its modules change over time; here is the current picture.
  3. First-round interviews. Usually two or three interviews, each combining a Personal Experience Interview and a case.
  4. Final-round interviews. A similar format with more senior interviewers, often partners.
  5. Offer.

The Personal Experience Interview (PEI)

Each interview includes a deep conversation about one real moment from your life. The interviewer asks follow-up questions, often many, to understand exactly what you did, thought and felt. McKinsey's own interviewing page suggests preparing personal examples you can talk about at length, in a conversational style.

The PEI is weighted as heavily as the case, so do not treat it as a warm-up. Prepare several detailed stories, each with clear actions you personally took. How to build your stories.

The case: interviewer-led

McKinsey cases are usually interviewer-led. Rather than you steering, the interviewer asks a sequence of questions: a structure, then perhaps a chart, a calculation, a brainstorm and a final recommendation. Each question is scored. Practise answering one well-defined question at a time, with a clear structure and a "so what" at the end.

How to prepare

  • Do McKinsey's official practice cases on its interviewing page.
  • Practise interviewer-led cases with a partner, where they ask specific questions in order.
  • Prepare and rehearse PEI stories out loud, and ask a friend to probe with "why?" and "what exactly did you do?"
  • Practise mental maths and chart reading daily for Solve and the cases.

Watch out for scams

McKinsey states that its recruiting never involves interviewing by instant message or asking candidates to pay for anything.

Sources

  • McKinsey: Interviewing
  • IGotAnOffer: McKinsey interview process
  • Hacking the Case Interview: McKinsey associate interview

Checked November 2026. Processes change by office and year, so always confirm with the firm's own careers page and your recruiter.
